headline: Norway's Lucky Strike Ends Brazil's Wasteful Dominance
story: Brazil pressed high and created chances but couldn't finish. Dominating through aggression (5.2 high-press phases), they forced Norway into a defensive crouch, yet failed to convert a glorious 0.79-xG opportunity at 14 minutes and squandered another 0.56-xG chance at 59. Norway, meanwhile, absorbed pressure with clinical ruthlessness, recovering the ball in just 16 seconds on average. The match hinged on conversion: Brazil's wastefulness against Norway's improbable precision.

Statistical chaos decided it. Brazil generated 2.57 xG to Norway's 1.41, yet lost 1-2. Erling Haaland's 8.7 rating dominated; his movement carved open spaces Brazil's 25.2-second ball recovery couldn't exploit. Norway's 79th-minute goal (0.08 xG) and the 90th-minute clincher (0.04 xG) were frankly miraculous finishes. Brazil's consolation at 90+10 (0.79 xG) arrived too late—a reminder that dominating the territory without clinical finishing is merely entertaining defeat.

keyMoment.text: Norway's 0.04-xG finish: impossible odds, perfect execution.

home.verdict: Pressed brilliantly but couldn't kill; two gilt-edged misses cost a quarter-final spot.
points: Squandered 0.79-xG chance at 14 mins (Saved) and 0.56-xG miss at 59; clinical finishing wins tournaments

away.verdict: Converted miracle finishes but survived Brazil's wasteful dominance—next foe won't be so forgiving.
points: Haaland's 8.7 rating controlled the match; yet Brazil missed sitters; next opponent will punish that
16.0-second ball recovery vs Brazil's 25.2 won transitions; 9 shots, 5 on target shows brutal efficiency

statLine: Brazil squandered 2.57 xG across 14 shots; Norway won with two finishes worth 0.12 xG combined.
